neighbours.label: futility idioms: ' point' / ' use' / ' bother' in 'no point (in)', 'no use', 'don't bother', meaning an action is pointless
fire: Honestly, there's no point in arguing with him about politics.
She knew it was no use crying over the broken vase.
After the third delay we saw there was little point in waiting.
Tenants say it's no use asking the landlord to fix anything.
Why bother washing the car if it's going to rain tomorrow?
Frankly, I don't see the point of rewriting the report again.
We told our cousin not to bother bringing a gift.
With a toddler, there is really no point trying to reason.
quiet: Honestly, there's a good reason to argue with him about politics.
She knew how to use glue to mend the broken vase.
After the third delay we saw there was little chance of leaving.
Tenants say the landlord is supposed to fix anything that breaks.
Why wash the car by hand when the car wash is so cheap?
Frankly, I can see the point on the map where the river bends.
We told our cousin to bring a gift for the host.
With a toddler, every walk ends with pointing at dogs.
